activity_context.topic_title: Jordan Canonical Form of a 3x3 Matrix

feedback.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 6 & 0 \\ -3 & -7 & 0 \\ 9 & 9 & 8\end{aligned}]
$$

The matrix above has eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=8,$ ${\lambda }_{2}=-1,$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=-4.$ Find a Jordan canonical form of the matrix.
feedback.worked_solution:
Notice that we are given a $3\times 3$ matrix that has precisely $3$ distinct eigenvalues. 

Therefore, $A$ is diagonalizable, and its Jordan canonical form is

$$
{J}_{1}(8)\,⊕\,{J}_{1}(-1)\,⊕\,{J}_{1}(-4)=[\begin{aligned}8 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -4\end{aligned}].
$$

**Note:** The Jordan canonical form is unique up to the order of the Jordan blocks.
